layers.title: Market data and reference
layers.requirement: Acquire licensed, source-identifiable US-equity observations; preserve feed, timestamps, identity and corporate actions; produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots and reject data whose historical availability or eligibility is unknown.
layers.current_choice: Official alpaca-py for the bounded selected market-data path; EdgarTools for selected filing parsing/acquisition; DuckDB and Parquet for local analysis; exchange_calendars for explicit session semantics. layers.rationale: Derived from domain row data-research (2026-09-22): Native acquisition, parsing and analytical receipts support these concrete interfaces without a new lake, broker or distributed database. They do not close the actual research bottleneck: a complete point-in-time eligible universe with trustworthy availability, identity and corporate-action semantics. Source-review defaults for DVC/Pandera must not be mistaken for installed acceptance. Databento/Massive are credible conditional alternatives when required coverage or rights cannot be obtained through the selected path.
limitations: The authenticated Alpaca receipt covers 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions over five successful pages, not a survivorship-free universe, complete history or real-time feed entitlement.

The temporal gates are project code (catalyst.py, security-identity/ledger.py), not upstream SDK capabilities. Transport also uses pinned private _session/_retry seams (authenticated-data receipt lines 215-218).

The c13 evidence covers one hardcoded XNYS session (summarize_backtest.py line 30) and a 104-session date check that does not prove row or market coverage. Holidays, early closes, halts and extended hours are untested. The 4.13.2 version is inferred from requirements.txt and stack.json; data/receipt.json does not record it.
Licensing and redistribution rights for the Alpaca SIP data are not established. The historical SIP response does not establish real-time access or entitlements (authenticated-data receipt line 223).

layers.verdict_overturn_when:
Four checks could change this verdict.

1. A retained blueprints/us-equities/ receipt shows c14 Databento (or another feed) acquiring consolidated bars and corporate actions for the same representative securities with raw-page sha256 hashes. The securities must include a delisting, the FB/META alias case and an AAPL split/dividend with a known currency. The rows must pass the same cutoff gate (security-identity/ledger.py select returns count 0 before observation) and close c9's open gaps: delisting, dividend currency and action coverage. That would replace or join c9. The reverse also counts: a rerun of blueprints/us-equities/alpaca-historical/collect.py verify or authenticated-data/compare.py that no longer reproduces 25/25 equal closes or the recorded page sha256 values would demote c9.
2. Rerunning `python3 -m unittest tests.test_security_identity tests.test_alpaca_historical tests.test_catalyst_provenance` could fail. Separately, the private-run commands recorded in the receipts could fail to reproduce their recorded results. For ledger.py select, those are counts 0/0/2 and their selected_rows_sha256 values. For catalyst.py packet --as-of 2020-03-03T00:00:00Z, the result is before_first_availability 5. Either outcome would demote c9 or c6. These reruns need host-private $ACQUISITION_RUN/$IDENTITY_LEDGER artifacts; the unit tests alone use offline fixtures.
3. summarize_backtest.py hardcodes session 2013-10-07 (line 30), so it cannot test new dates. The runnable c13 check is `python3 -c "import exchange_calendars as x; c=x.get_calendar('XNYS'); [print(d, c.is_session(d), c.session_close(d) if c.is_session(d) else None) for d in ('2013-07-04','2013-11-29','2013-12-24')]"` under exchange-calendars 4.13.2. Its output would be compared with the NYSE-published 2013 holiday and early-close schedule. A mismatch would demote c13.
4. The comparison in the packet's existing_overturn_when is still unexecuted. Once run, it should replace this sample-bounded verdict.

layers.title: Storage and compute
layers.requirement: Acquire licensed, source-identifiable US-equity observations; preserve feed, timestamps, identity and corporate actions; produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots and reject data whose historical availability or eligibility is unknown.
layers.current_choice: Official alpaca-py for the bounded selected market-data path; EdgarTools for selected filing parsing/acquisition; DuckDB and Parquet for local analysis; exchange_calendars for explicit session semantics. Dataset manifests and schema checks are requirements, while DVC/Pandera remain source-reviewed implementation candidates.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row data-research (2026-09-22): Native acquisition, parsing and analytical receipts support these concrete interfaces without a new lake, broker or distributed database. They do not close the actual research bottleneck: a complete point-in-time eligible universe with trustworthy availability, identity and corporate-action semantics. Source-review defaults for DVC/Pandera must not be mistaken for installed acceptance. Databento/Massive are credible conditional alternatives when required coverage or rights cannot be obtained through the selected path.
limitations: The authenticated Alpaca receipt covers 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions over five successful pages, not a survivorship-free universe, complete history or real-time feed entitlement.

Numeric corporate-action values matched the frozen probe, but missing dividend currency prevented full cash-unit reconciliation. Original historical availability and complete action coverage remain open.
Three documentary lifecycle cases preserve observed cutoffs and source anchors; retrospective claims do not establish historical as-known eligibility or permanent security identity.
The prior SEC HTTP 403 remains a historical failure. Later corrected acquisition and parsing qualify their selected requests only; no general filing-completeness or strategy-validity claim follows.
SQL, schemas and content hashes cannot repair missing provenance, revised fundamentals, access rights or outcome-selected samples.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under foundation-memory (1), agents-operations (1); data-research (11) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Freeze required universe/history/latency, rights, correction and availability semantics; compare selected providers on representative securities including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, then change the feed/store only when a candidate closes those gaps with auditable records and acceptable measured cost. Add a server or lake only after local throughput/concurrency measurements justify it.

winners.why_selected:
DuckDB (c4) is the only storage/compute candidate here with retained native execution evidence. I checked each point below against the source files myself.

(1) blueprints/us-equities/data/receipt.json (kind native_cli_e2e, recorded 2026-09-19) records one native run of blueprints/us-equities/data/summarize_backtest.py. The script refuses to overwrite an existing Parquet file (lines 17-18). It casts fillPrice and fillQuantity to DECIMAL(20, 8) (lines 22-24), writes zstd Parquet, reads the file back, and records SHA-256 hashes for both the source and the Parquet. The run produced events 6, distinct_orders 3, statuses filled 3 / submitted 3, calendar XNYS, sample_session 2013-10-07 and parquet_sha256 48ec550a96771e284bde09f6793b0d064e47bf3a731d8a1ac389a509b616f66d.

(2) blueprints/us-equities/research-runtime/receipt.json records the same parquet_sha256 at line 53. At lines 43-46 its Dagu step order_table is 'succeeded', and blueprints/us-equities/research-runtime/prepare-evidence.yaml lines 9-10 show that this step runs summarize_backtest.py. The final_validation_exit_codes [0, 0] at lines 38-41 belong to the two Dagu YAML validations, not to the order_table step. Two recorded runs therefore produced identical Parquet bytes on this bundled input.

(3) blueprints/us-equities/financial-data/receipt.json records duckdb_version 1.5.5 and research_environment_suite tests 84, failures 0, skips 0. It also records native_roundtrip: 'Exact DECIMAL(38,12) values including 12345678901234567890123456.123456789012 survive Parquet and the packet CLI'. Those checks used synthetic fixtures.

(4) blueprints/us-equities/workers/requirements.txt pins duckdb==1.5.5, which matches the packet pin v1.5.5.

Scope: DuckDB is selected only as the embedded SQL/Parquet engine for exact, hash-identified, reproducible research snapshots. The evidence does not show acquisition of licensed observations, preservation of corporate actions, or rejection of data whose historical availability is unknown. Pandera (c8) now has retained, executed fail-closed gate results, but only on synthetic 0-4-row fixtures, so it stays conditional (see alternatives). This is my own source review of the local receipts. No TypeSafe inference was supplied or run, and I did not use any withheld packet decision fields.

Six result files sit in blueprints/us-equities/data/fixtures/, and four of them are cited here: good-gate-result.json (status pass, row_count 4), bad-gate-result.json (status fail, row_count 4, checked_at 2026-09-22T15:12:36.900809+00:00, failing valid_trading_session, volume_integral_non_negative, observed_at_not_future, high_ge_max_open_close and unique_symbol_session), null-price-cell-gate-result.json (fail, row_count 2) and empty-snapshot-gate-result.json (fail, row_count 0). Every result records pandera 0.33.1, which matches the packet pin. catalogs/us-equities/gates-20260922.json lines 66-81 classify the gate as evidence_class 'synthetic' and say 'No real snapshot ingest exists yet'. tests/test_promotion_gate.py reruns the fixtures (lines 142-239), but it is skipUnless the isolated venv exists (lines 90-91). The packet card limitation calling fail-closed promotion 'still implementation work' (packet line 234) is therefore outdated for the synthetic case. Pandera still does not join the winner set. And the gate's fixed CHECK_NAMES (promotion_gate.py lines 45-49) contain no historical availability, eligibility or corporate-action check, only observed_at not in the future.

The packet evidence is one upstream README, which I did not open. c4 already writes and rereads the Parquet with native, hash-identified results. pyarrow 25.0.1 appears in the gate results' versions field only as an environment dependency. Arrow is not a separate default until a round-trip receipt shows a precision or time-unit need that DuckDB does not meet.

layers.title: Data quality and orchestration
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under data-research (2); agents-operations (7) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

candidates.name: Loki

candidates.name: Grafana

winners.why_selected:

layers.title: Research, factors and ML
layers.requirement: Use the selected NautilusTrader destination with broker-specific execution boundaries, deterministic numeric risk and reproducible equity accounting; preserve the prior LEAN oracle and qualify any strategy with causal data, costs and independent reconciliation.
layers.current_choice: NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 is the user-selected destination; LEAN remains the retained historical comparison engine. Nautilus native IBKR awaits broker acceptance; Alpaca uses official alpaca-py and a separately qualified deterministic paper path. No strategy is promoted as profitable.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row engines-strategies (2026-09-22): The current choice follows the explicit runtime target and supported native IBKR direction, with real installation/replay and bounded AAPL accounting evidence. LEAN has deeper retained SPY stress/dividend/cash evidence and is kept as the comparison oracle rather than relabeled a losing engine. The AAPL diagnostic and one Alpaca paper roundtrip do not prove SPY parity, realistic liquidity, IBKR operation, continuous paper service or a winning strategy. Existing research modules remain task-specific.
limitations: Nautilus 2.0.0rc5 is a prerelease. The old September 19 Nautilus alternative and LEAN default cards remain historical; runtime-target.json governs the current destination.

The retained AAPL replay has 15 bars and five roundtrips per baseline/stress scenario with reconciled cash; it excludes known action dates and uses retrospective synthetic close fills with unlimited modeled depth.
SPY/LEAN dividend/cash parity is still planned. LEAN's known-crash fixtures are engineering stresses, not untouched holdout results or calibrated broker execution.

The Alpaca trial observed two actual writes, a -0.08 USD cash-matched gross result, flat/idle reconciliation and completed-trial recovery with zero additional writes. In-flight native failure cases, IBKR, live operation and continuous paper operation remain open.
No accepted point-in-time universe, extreme-mover/catalyst strategy, financing-inclusive performance or deployable profitability follows from these receipts.

Independent source review found two bare matches! expressions that do not assert denial-event variants in Nautilus risk tests, also present in v2.0.0rc5 source. Other tests assert denial and reasons. This narrow test defect is not an observed runtime failure; see docs/blind-catalog-source-adjudication-20260921.md.

The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under data-research (12), foundation-memory (6), agents-operations (5); engines-strategies (23) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Reopen the implementation choice if Nautilus cannot preserve a required cash/order semantic, fails a preregistered SPY/LEAN parity tolerance, or a broker-specific adapter cannot pass ownership, reconciliation, partial/cancel/reconnect and numeric risk cases. Compare alternatives on the same frozen inputs and failure contract; promote a strategy only after independent temporal and cost-aware evaluation.

layers.verdict_overturn_when:
The verdict changes when an executed receipt shows one of the following:

(a) inspect-ai 0.3.266 fails the next acceptance recorded at catalogs/convergence-practice/architecture-wave/UKGovernmentBEIS__inspect_ai.json line 123: "One mock-model task with deterministic scoring, bounded concurrency/retries, retained failure log, interruption and resume; no provider request." Retained evidence does not establish that a no-provider model backend exists in the pinned release; that must be observed.

(b) A local sqlite MLflow run cannot read back the parameters, metrics and FAILED status it recorded. This command is this lane's own derived check. It is not the catalog snippet: data-research.json line 801 only logs a param and a metric and prints the tracking URI.
python3 -c "import tempfile, mlflow; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); mlflow.set_tracking_uri('sqlite:///'+d+'/m.db'); mlflow.set_experiment('x'); r=mlflow.start_run(); mlflow.log_param('k','v'); mlflow.log_metric('m',1); mlflow.end_run(status='FAILED'); g=mlflow.get_run(r.info.run_id); print(g.info.status, dict(g.data.params), dict(g.data.metrics))"
It passes only if the output shows FAILED together with param k=v and metric m=1.

(c) Phoenix arize-phoenix-v20.14.0 alone passes the full check set, in a credential-free environment: deterministic evaluation, failed-attempt retention, parameter and metric readback, interruption and resume, and no provider calls. Phoenix doing this with one component where the winners need two would overturn the verdict.

It would also overturn if any other adopted candidate passes the same checks with fewer components. Record such a result in the same receipt shape as blueprints/convergence-practice/arb-trace2code/receipt.json. That file is a shape template only; it contains no evaluation-experiments task.

layers.title: Agents, models and workers
layers.requirement: Keep durable project knowledge, exact code and dated financial sources retrievable across native clients, with source recovery, explicit project scope and measurable retrieval quality.
layers.current_choice: ai-memory as the shared memory of record; QMD BM25 for documents; Serena for exact symbols; SocratiCode with Qdrant for conceptual code search; Context Mode and RTK for selected large outputs. These are complementary lanes, not one benchmark winner.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row foundation-memory (2026-09-22): The selected lanes have native operation and recovery evidence on the existing host and avoid making every lookup depend on another extraction model or service. The measured QMD domain fixture returned the intended source in the first three results for 8 of 12 queries, so its low setup cost supports retention while the four misses require a representative comparison before claiming retrieval superiority. Memory recall and code search receipts do not qualify financial answer truth or historical market availability.
limitations: Twelve curated queries are a bounded diagnostic, not an independent holdout or a complete financial RAG evaluation. Exact-source recall at three was 8/12; misses remain recorded.

The eight native answer invocations form four within-provider task comparisons; two Claude full-context answers missed the word protocol and one focused Codex answer scored 9.5 versus 10. These are not general or causal savings results.
Same-host encrypted restore preserved application state, but independent key recovery, off-host durability and new-host client rebinding remain unqualified.
Alternative memory and RAG repositories below were generally source-reviewed, not run head-to-head. A source-only candidate has not failed.

Current primary-source review corrects manual-only, Claude-only and cloud-only exclusions. No matched memory benchmark or new installation was run; automatic capture, local providers and published scores remain source claims until exercised on the selected profile.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under agents-operations (10); foundation-memory (28) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Run a preregistered, representative held-out financial/document and code retrieval set at the same context budget; replace or supplement a lane only if a candidate improves source/answer fidelity, abstention and measured task cost while preserving isolation, exact source recovery and native client behavior.

candidates.name: ai-memory
candidates.rationale: Retain one shared project-scoped memory system because native capture/retrieval, maintenance and restoration have direct historical evidence. The fresh upstream source pin is review-only and does not replace the installed pin. This is the best-supported current operational fit, not a demonstrated recall, learning or cost winner.

candidates.name: QMD
candidates.rationale: The local BM25 lane requires no model weights and has native search/get/update evidence. Its 8/12 exact-source recall at three bounds the claim; retention remains conditional on a representative comparison.

candidates.name: Serena
candidates.rationale: Language-server symbol/reference retrieval fits exact source editing; native Python/TypeScript coverage was repaired and exercised. This complements document and semantic search instead of replacing them.

candidates.name: SocratiCode
candidates.rationale: Native indexing, watcher and conceptual retrieval already use the scoped local embedding service. Keep that operational path while acknowledging hardware, licensing and reindexing requirements.

candidates.name: Qdrant
candidates.rationale: The vector store is already integrated with the selected semantic lane. A native snapshot/restore preserved five collections, 201 points and one exact query; that is operational evidence, not comparative retrieval quality.

candidates.name: Context Mode
candidates.rationale: Useful native calls retain large output outside the prompt and retrieve focused sections. Counters are connection-level estimates; native use and retained recovery do not establish avoided provider billing.

candidates.name: RTK
candidates.rationale: Supported CLI filtering has clean-userspace and hosted Linux fixture evidence, including raw proxy fidelity and error retention. It is selected for matching outputs, not an automatic filter for every source.

candidates.name: Mem0
candidates.rationale: The current project provides application user/session/agent memory and temporal retrieval with published reproducible evaluation references. It is a serious application-memory candidate; a same-task project-continuity and cost comparison remains absent, and benchmark claims do not transfer automatically.

candidates.name: Hindsight
candidates.rationale: Priority comparison for retain/recall/reflect and temporal or experiential memory. Current upstream explicitly documents local providers and native Codex/Claude subscription providers, so missing API credentials alone is not a valid exclusion. Published benchmarks are not a matched test of our project recall, source fidelity, boundaries or operating cost.

candidates.name: OpenViking
candidates.rationale: Hierarchical context filesystem unifies resources, memory and skills with scoped retrieval and inspectable session-derived Markdown. Consider it if fragmented context becomes a measured obstacle; published benchmarks and the AGPL deployment model need workload-specific evaluation before replacing current scoped lanes.

candidates.name: Graphiti
candidates.rationale: Temporal entity relationships are relevant to dated issuer/security research. This is a potential complementary graph or memory challenger, not evidence that a graph supplies missing source availability or improves the existing project wiki; qualify extraction provenance, updates, isolation and restore on the intended corpus.

candidates.name: Haystack
candidates.rationale: The reviewed explicit pipeline framework is a candidate when financial document ingestion/evaluation needs an application RAG layer. It is not needed merely to wrap already working native retrieval.

candidates.name: LightRAG
candidates.rationale: Graph-assisted cross-document retrieval is relevant, but no matched financial-source evaluation establishes gains over the current lexical/semantic lanes. Unqualified does not mean an observed failure.

candidates.name: LlamaIndex
candidates.rationale: Use a specific maintained connector or pipeline when it removes a demonstrated integration gap. Broad package adoption would add overlap without a current task comparison.

candidates.name: Docling
candidates.rationale: Layout-aware PDF/table/OCR extraction addresses documents outside lightweight HTML conversion. It needs document-specific fidelity and resource checks before being the default ingestion path.

candidates.name: Headroom
candidates.rationale: Compression may fit selected API-worker artifacts, but the catalog's proxy/SDK route is source review and must preserve trading evidence, tool structure and cache behavior. Existing offline artifact checks are a separate scope.

candidates.name: Basic Memory
candidates.rationale: Priority comparison for human-editable Markdown knowledge and cross-client MCP. The current Claude plugin documents session-start briefings, pre-compaction checkpoints and opt-in capture; it is not only manual notes. Qualify its AGPL deployment fit, actual capture, project isolation and restored state before migrating the authoritative store.

candidates.name: Claude-mem
candidates.rationale: Persistent capture, compression and retrieval are a direct comparison candidate. The pinned README includes OpenCode and other integrations beyond Claude, plus distinct hosted/local observer choices; do not dismiss it as Claude-only. Compare capture fidelity, identity boundaries, provider behavior and migration before running overlapping capture stores.

candidates.name: Letta Code
candidates.rationale: Active stateful agent harness with persistent memory/skills and documented local/cloud backends. It is a broader runtime-and-memory architecture, not only a drop-in store. The legacy Letta repository redirects to it while V1 remains on an archive branch; compare native-account behavior, recall, lifecycle and migration before replacement.

candidates.name: Cognee
candidates.rationale: Source-reviewed graph/context candidate for documents, code and conversations. The upstream explicitly offers local extraction and embeddings without a cloud API key, while its default LLM recipe uses OpenAI; choose and qualify the actual profile rather than treating the product as cloud-only or automatically offline.

candidates.name: Supermemory
candidates.rationale: Application memory/profile/search candidate with documented local server, local embeddings and an Ollama offline route. Cloud-only exclusion is stale. Confirm the selected implementation's provider calls, licensing/dependencies, export/restore, isolation and representative retrieval before adopting another authoritative memory service.

alternatives.name: foundation-codebase-memory-mcp
alternatives.why_not_default: This is a static-graph exact-code fallback. It has runs in both client families, but only through bridges. evidence/receipts/native-cli-gaps.json records native Claude running search_graph and trace_path through MCPorter with status passed, returning collect at lines 91-127 with 4 callees. The native Codex CLI follow-up there was blocked_before_tools by usage_limit_exceeded. evidence/receipts/desktop-cli-workflows.json (lines 11 and 25-41) records the active Codex Desktop task running static graph search and trace with search_exit 0 and trace_exit 0. It returned collect in tools/ecosystem/linux-usage-report.cjs at lines 91-127 with callees installation, sourcesFor, runParser and overlaps, and runtime_execution_trace false. evidence/receipts/component-history.json (lines 249-251) records native_claude and native_codex as 'not independently demonstrated' and current_desktop as a 'Root CLI bridge'. So c14 has no native MCP registration proof, its static edges do not prove runtime execution, and it overlaps c9 and c12 for exact code. A head-to-head against c9 on exact-symbol recall has not been run.

alternatives.name: Qdrant
alternatives.why_not_default: Qdrant is the vector store behind c12, not a separate retrieval interface. evidence/receipts/native-rag.json shows collection codebase_72cfa87c5abf with status green, reached through SocratiCode. component-history.json records it as a supporting local service. Its card states that no financial-document corpus exists yet. Selecting c12 already includes it.

alternatives.name: Context Mode
alternatives.why_not_default: Context Mode ran in both clients: native-context-memory.json fresh_startup records ctx_execute, and observability/restart-receipt.json records 11 tools and 14 successful results. It executes large outputs and returns bounded results, which does not make it a durable project-knowledge or code retrieval store. blueprints/us-equities/workers/receipt.json records ctx_execute_file failing in the SDK worker on the project-root restriction, with a scoped override blocked by the approval policy. estimated_tokens_saved was 0 in workers/receipt.json and restart-receipt.json.

alternatives.name: vllm
alternatives.why_not_default: vLLM is a runtime dependency that serves c12's local embeddings, not a retrieval layer. evidence/receipts/vllm-compatibility.json shows 0.29.0 installed but failing GPU startup with 'RuntimeError: UVA is not available' on the WSL host. 0.25.0 was restored, and desktop-direct-rag.json records active_model_service_version 0.25.0 with retrieval passing. The packet's upstream v0.30.0 is untested.

alternatives.name: foundation-repomix
alternatives.why_not_default: Repomix builds selected-file handoff bundles only. evidence/receipts/portable-cli-artifacts.json records one standalone CLI fixture pack (repomix_contains_selected_paths true) and says it is 'not an LLM invocation'. component-history.json records native Claude and Codex use as 'not independently demonstrated' and one lossy artifact at 3679→645 o200k tokens. The output is not a retrievable index and has no quality measure. I corrected the evidence class to synthetic because only a fixture CLI run is retained.

alternatives.name: foundation-toon
alternatives.why_not_default: TOON is a serialization format, not retrieval. portable-cli-artifacts.json records one standalone encode/decode fixture roundtrip (toon_roundtrip_equal true) that is 'not an LLM invocation'. component-history.json says it is not independently demonstrated in native clients, and a nested fixture grew from 69 to 94 tokens. I corrected the evidence class to synthetic.

alternatives.name: RTK
alternatives.why_not_default: RTK compacts command output and does not retrieve knowledge. The native hook and explicit calls passed (component-history.json id rtk; native-context-memory.json 'rtk git log -6' exit 0). The only measure is a lossy artifact count of 533→176 tokens (artifact-reductions.json historical_rtk), which is not a retrieval-quality result.

alternatives.name: codex-native-sdk
alternatives.why_not_default: This is the evidenced worker runtime that matches the layer title, but it does not meet the stated retrieval requirement. blueprints/us-equities/workers/receipt.json records one completed research turn that read receipts through Context Mode ctx_execute. ctx_execute_file failed, and the configured model is not independent provider attestation. policy.md delegates retrieval to the QMD, Serena, SocratiCode, ai-memory and Context Mode lanes.

alternatives.name: codex-acp
alternatives.why_not_default: This is an ACP worker adapter. deerflow/research-receipt.json records one embedded prompt that completed, but the 'read-only' mode maps to workspaceWrite/on-request. The receipt says no memory/RAG integration was exercised.

alternatives.name: deerflow
alternatives.why_not_default: DeerFlow is an optional research host. native-receipt.json shows memory disabled and the discovery database running in memory. research-receipt.json records one invoke_acp_agent prompt with no planner, UI or standing service, and states that no memory/RAG integration or durable recovery was exercised.

alternatives.name: omniroute
alternatives.why_not_default: OmniRoute is a provider gateway, not retrieval. health-receipt.json holds status-only HTTP 200 checks. astra-receipt.json and routing/README.md record one Astra text response of 136 tokens after an initial HTTP 400 and an HTTP 499. The README says tools, compaction and worker parity remain unproved.

alternatives.name: langgraph
alternatives.why_not_default: LangGraph provides an agent-state graph, not retrieval. Its only evidence is a source-review URL, which I did not open. Its card says the import is an installation smoke test only and that InMemorySaver loses state on restart.

alternatives.name: foundation-pageindex
alternatives.why_not_default: PageIndex is the only candidate whose role targets document and financial retrieval, but its evidence is a source-review URL only. I did not open it, and nothing was run on a financial corpus. The pin is behind upstream (v0.2.18 vs v0.2.19). Untested does not mean it failed.

alternatives.name: Graphiti
alternatives.why_not_default: Graphiti's evidence is source review only (URLs, not opened). The card says there is no graph deployment and no extraction-accuracy proof. Dated sourced relationships would fit the financial-source part of the requirement, but nothing was executed.

alternatives.name: foundation-pgvector
alternatives.why_not_default: pgvector's evidence is source review only (URL, not opened). The card says a build is not extension activation and that it adds no benefit over the current Qdrant index without an established SQL integration need.

alternatives.name: foundation-agent-retrieval-bench

domain_rows.title: Scoped memory and research retrieval
domain_rows.requirement: Keep durable project knowledge, exact code and dated financial sources retrievable across native clients, with source recovery, explicit project scope and measurable retrieval quality.
domain_rows.current_choice: ai-memory as the shared memory of record; QMD BM25 for documents; Serena for exact symbols; SocratiCode with Qdrant for conceptual code search; Context Mode and RTK for selected large outputs. These are complementary lanes, not one benchmark winner.
domain_rows.rationale: The selected lanes have native operation and recovery evidence on the existing host and avoid making every lookup depend on another extraction model or service. The measured QMD domain fixture returned the intended source in the first three results for 8 of 12 queries, so its low setup cost supports retention while the four misses require a representative comparison before claiming retrieval superiority. Memory recall and code search receipts do not qualify financial answer truth or historical market availability.
limitations: Twelve curated queries are a bounded diagnostic, not an independent holdout or a complete financial RAG evaluation. Exact-source recall at three was 8/12; misses remain recorded.

The eight native answer invocations form four within-provider task comparisons; two Claude full-context answers missed the word protocol and one focused Codex answer scored 9.5 versus 10. These are not general or causal savings results.
Same-host encrypted restore preserved application state, but independent key recovery, off-host durability and new-host client rebinding remain unqualified.
Alternative memory and RAG repositories below were generally source-reviewed, not run head-to-head. A source-only candidate has not failed.

Current primary-source review corrects manual-only, Claude-only and cloud-only exclusions. No matched memory benchmark or new installation was run; automatic capture, local providers and published scores remain source claims until exercised on the selected profile.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Run a preregistered, representative held-out financial/document and code retrieval set at the same context budget; replace or supplement a lane only if a candidate improves source/answer fidelity, abstention and measured task cost while preserving isolation, exact source recovery and native client behavior.

No accepted point-in-time universe, extreme-mover/catalyst strategy, financing-inclusive performance or deployable profitability follows from these receipts.

candidates.rationale: The official SDK has a separately implemented bounded deterministic paper lifecycle and one reconciled long-to-flat trial. It is not a native Nautilus Alpaca adapter and must retain one owned writer.

candidates.name: LEAN Alpaca brokerage
candidates.rationale: Native patched adapter compilation is retained evidence, but initialization/account entitlement and this adapter's paper execution remain unqualified. The separate alpaca-py smoke does not close its gate or restore the historical default route.

candidates.name: Lumibot
candidates.rationale: A direct Python strategy lifecycle with Alpaca support is a substantial alternative. It needs the same data, risk, order/recovery and accounting comparison before replacing the selected destination.

candidates.name: vectorbt
candidates.rationale: Array-based sweeps can accelerate a defined research task, subject to semantics and license fit. Selected signals would still require event-driven accounting and execution checks; no matched speed/quality result is recorded here.

candidates.name: Backtrader
candidates.rationale: Useful for an existing strategy or bounded offline comparison; its reviewed integration age weakens the case for a new second Alpaca host. No general engine failure was measured.

candidates.name: backtesting.py
candidates.rationale: Small OHLC prototypes fit signal sanity checks, but do not meet the selected portfolio order-state and reconciliation-host requirement by themselves.

candidates.name: Zipline Reloaded
candidates.rationale: Maintained continuation is relevant for existing Zipline/Pipeline research. It has no recorded same-input advantage that warrants a second active event engine in this stack.

candidates.name: ib_async
candidates.rationale: IBKR is now selected, so the old 'only if later selected' rationale is historical. This community client remains an alternative to the selected native Nautilus adapter, with no local broker/recovery comparison establishing a need to switch.

candidates.name: skfolio
candidates.rationale: Native 1.2.9 WalkForward evaluation produced 20 development folds and one reserved period with causality assertions. This qualifies a raw-price label control module, not portfolio PnL, optimization superiority or broker risk enforcement.

candidates.name: Qlib
candidates.rationale: A structured factor/model experiment framework can help after a defensible US point-in-time dataset exists. Its broader workflow does not cure the current provenance/eligibility gaps or justify another active strategy stack yet.

candidates.name: FinRL
candidates.rationale: RL remains an experiment after deterministic and supervised baselines; no local out-of-sample, cost-aware strategy or execution qualification supports promoting it.

candidates.name: TradingAgents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed multi-agent financial analysis workflow is a research candidate. More agents and a simulated decision pipeline do not establish causal data, alpha or authority to bypass deterministic order/risk code.

candidates.name: PyPortfolioOpt
candidates.rationale: A smaller classical allocation module can be preferable when allocation alone is required. The selected skfolio study qualifies chronological evaluation, not a head-to-head proof that its optimizers dominate this candidate.

candidates.name: Dockerized IB Gateway
